data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'Khasi' which means 'The One Who Gives Joy', this name is perfect for a child who brings happiness and joy to those around them. It's a beautiful and meaningful name for a baby boy or girl. The name Khashi carries the meaning “Joy, Happiness” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Pashto. Parents who choose Khashi usually hope their child will grow to embody joy, happiness and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Battuta's Travels: During his journey through Central Asia and China, Ibn Battuta encountered the Khashi people in the fifth decade of the 14th century. He described them as nomads who lived in tents, primarily in the region of Kashgar in modern-day Xinjiang, China.

The Annals of Samarkand by Abulfeda: In the late 14th century, during the reign of Amir Temur (Timur), the Khashi people were mentioned as rebellious subjects who lived in the region of Kashgar in what is now present-day Uzbekistan. They were reportedly subdued by the forces of Amir Temur in 1369 or 1370.
